verdict.rationale: Open WebUI documents concrete permission/approval controls — a per-chat tool approval mode with Allow/Deny buttons on pending tool actions (docs-13, docs-37), RBAC roles/trust levels (docs-17, docs-47), and an air-gapped/network-isolated deployment mode (docs-18). However, its own docs state that Tools/Functions/Pipes/Filters/Pipelines 'execute arbitrary Python code on your server' (docs-25) with no mention of container or VM sandboxing to isolate that execution, so containment relies on approval gates and RBAC rather than true sandboxed execution. Missing for 10: documented container/VM sandbox isolation for tool/code execution, granular per-tool policy restrictions (e.g., filesystem/network allowlists), and independent verification that approval/RBAC controls hold up in practice.
